text.p: Following are the main stories in Thursday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
All dailies lead with the freeing of hostages from the besieged Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima, Peru on Tuesday.
-- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said the U.S. should not impose economic sanctions against Burma, and that Asean would work hard towards making the country part of the regional grouping.
-- The Anti-Corruption Agency detained two Royal Customs and Excise officials for allegedly accepting money to reduce duties on imported telecommunications equipment from Singapore.
-- Sarawak state's Land Development Minister Celestine Ujang resigned on Wednesday, three days after his election to a state assembly post was nullified by an election court.
-- The government has not issued any "buy" directive to large local institutional funds to support falling share prices, said Treasury Secretary General Clifford Herbert.
